answers.answer: Open Overlays in the sidebar and choose New overlay, type a name in Name, choose a Code language or keep Vue, then choose Create overlay. The new overlay opens beside the list and has its address at once. To get the link, choose Copy browser source address on the open overlay (the button then reads Address copied), or use Connect and then Copy address in the OBS setup dialog. The page never shows the address itself.
answers.quote: Copy browser source address copies the address OBS needs.

answers.answer: You need one of the roles that may change overlays, which is stated in Who can use this page. A VIP can only view and copy, and cannot create. You also need OBS with a Browser source to show the output, which is stated in the opening paragraph. For the code path the language must be chosen up front, because it cannot be changed later (step 3).
answers.quote: A Moderator, Lead moderator, Editor or Broadcaster may open the page and change overlays.

answers.answer: After Create overlay the dialog closes and the overlay opens beside the list, switched on. After copying, the button reads Address copied. Once OBS has it open, the row turns green with A browser source is open, and Health says Events reach your stream. A custom overlay (Overlays page) is a different thing from a supplied source (OBS page, Required overlays).
answers.quote: The dialog closes and the new overlay opens beside the list, switched on.

answers.answer: Choose Duplicate on the open first overlay. The copy opens at once and starts switched on, with its own browser source address, so changing it does not alter the original. Paste the copy's address into a new OBS Browser source. The other way is to make a fresh overlay with New overlay. Duplicate only works when the original already has compiled code.
answers.quote: Choose Duplicate at the bottom of an open overlay.

answers.answer: I had to guess whether a brand-new overlay, which starts from a starter, already counts as having compiled code before any Save & Compile, so I could not tell whether Duplicate works on it right away. I would test it and read the error under the footer. Getting the link also has no numbered step: I learned it from the paragraph after the list and the later section on the open overlay. The cost is small because that paragraph comes right after the steps.
answers.quote: An overlay with no compiled code yet cannot be copied.

answers.answer: Read aloud, the permission sentence in Set the audio levels is hard to follow. It names a 'widget' permission the page never introduced (the VIP section later calls the area Widgets), so a listener has to rewind. Explaining Vue as a JavaScript framework for web pages is a little more than this reader needs, but it is short.
answers.quote: Audio levels follows the Sounds permission instead of the widget one: you need to read sounds to see it, and to change sounds to move its sliders.
